newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santos halted as stevedores join demo.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santos halted as stevedores join demo.

text.p: Brazil's key Santos port stopped loading and was expected to be paralyzed for two hours because most stevedores were attending a demonstration in the city center, a spokesman said.
"They have just stopped," the spokesman said, adding that he expected loading to resume at 1900 local/2200 GMT.
Twenty-four vessels have stopped operating and the port authority expects that 12,000 tonnes of product will not be loaded due to the demonstration.
This includes not only grains but also other types of cargoes such as orange juice. Only oil and chemical products were expected to continue loading because the process is automated for these goods.
The stevedores are protesting in front of the Santos mayor's office against the deadlock in talks with steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) following a strike last week.

Twenty-six stevedores have been occupying two vessels at Cosipa's private terminal at the port in protest against the firm's decision to use its own workers to conduct loading and unloading at the terminal.
The action has effectively paralyzed Cosipa's operations at the port. Military police officers are stationed on the pier but have so far failed to carry out a judge's order to evacuate the workers.

The stevedores said they would immediately call a port strike if the police tried to evict them or if Cosipa allowed any new vessels to dock at the terminal and tried to load or unload them with its own workers.
